mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for S&P 500 constituents and leads to negative returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% signals a dual shock of higher rates and inflation, eroding real corporate earnings and depressing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1 million units for four consecutive months signals a housing market downturn, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and drags on S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) is inconsistent and signals labor market confusion; this ambiguity increases market volatility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE also increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals reduced household buffer and impending consumption cutbacks, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month moving average for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.
